title: Safety-constrained multi-agent AI for emergency department disposition decisions
task: Multi-agent AI for emergency department admission/discharge decisions
key_results: Single LM agent superior to SMARTriage AI v2 (AUC 0.821–0.823 vs 0.794); apparent accuracy 88.2% but dropped to 65.0% without physician text; heavy optimization bias from development on evaluation cohort (30 cycles, no held-out set)
comments: Significant performance degradation without physician summary; development methodology severely compromises generalizability claims; external validation mandatory.

model_io.model: SMARTriage AI v1/v2 (multi-agent LM + deterministic rules) vs single LM agent

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-agent design with safety gates outperforms single-agent models
hypotheses.result: Rejected: redesigned v2 showed worse discrimination (AUC 0.794) than single LM agent (0.821–0.823)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Physician documentation enables higher-accuracy dispositions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: accuracy 97.2% with summary vs 78.2% without; 65.0% without physician text indicates severe documentation dependence

title: Modality-adaptive learning for glaucoma diagnosis with incomplete availability of fundus photographs and visual field data
task: Modality-adaptive glaucoma diagnosis with incomplete multimodal data
key_results: CGMA-Net achieved AUC 0.997, 97.6% accuracy, 98.9% sensitivity, 94.9% specificity; maintained high discrimination across fundus-only, VF-only, and paired modalities; gated fusion removal caused larger performance loss than removing cross-attention
comments: Excellent internal validation but retrospective cohort with participant-level splits; ambiguous cases and variable quality examinations require prospective validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gated adaptive fusion prevents absent modalities from degrading classification without imputation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: gated fusion essential; ablation showed larger performance decrease than cross-attention removal

hypotheses.hypothesis: Learned uncertainty and MC dropout uncertainty are higher for misclassified samples
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: both uncertainty measures correlated with classification errors

title: A feasibility study for resolving cellular populations in precision cancer medicine by integrating single-cell multiomics
task: Single-cell multiomics for subclonal resolution and treatment planning in advanced cancer
key_results: Resolved previously undetectable subclonal mutations and immune populations; tracked resistance mechanisms longitudinally; found treatment genes heterogeneously distributed across malignant clusters suggesting combinatorial regimens needed; some genes predicted targetable by bulk RNA-seq found predominantly in normal populations
comments: Feasibility study on 25 samples from 17 patients demonstrates proof-of-concept; clinical implementation utility requires prospective validation and larger cohorts.

inputs: tumor biopsies from BC Cancer Personalised OncoGenomics programme

hypotheses.hypothesis: Single-cell profiling resolves therapeutic resistance mechanisms undetectable by bulk sequencing
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: identified subclonal mutations, immune infiltration, and heterogeneous treatment-gene distribution

hypotheses.hypothesis: Targetable genes predicted by bulk RNA-seq may be expressed primarily in non-malignant populations
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: found genes presumed targetable predominantly in normal cell populations, not malignant clusters

title: Explainable spatiotemporal graph learning for early identification of localized infectious disease risk
task: Explainable spatiotemporal graph learning for localized infectious disease forecasting
key_results: STGCN-AG best at 3-day horizon, competitive at longer horizons; adaptive gating identifies when/where model modulates graph representations; offline models outperformed LSTM/trees but showed limited absolute performance degrading at longer horizons; online prequential evaluation showed lag and weaker responsiveness at longer horizons
comments: Limited absolute predictive performance and temporal degradation highlight challenges in longer-term localized forecasting; interpretability gains offset by accuracy limitations.

model_io.model: STGCN-AG (spatiotemporal graph CNN with adaptive gating) vs LSTM, tree-based, standard graph models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Adaptive gating mechanism improves spatiotemporal graph forecasting by contextual modulation
hypotheses.result: Partially confirmed: STGCN-AG best at 3-day horizon but performance degraded at longer horizons; gating interpretability improved but absolute accuracy remained limited

hypotheses.hypothesis: Explainable AI analysis of gating/sensitivity improves model interpretability for public health decisions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: adaptive gate identified dimensions, regions, and times of stronger modulation; interpretability enhanced but predictive limitations remain

title: Predicting spin-crossover behavior in metal-organic frameworks from limited and noisy data using quantile active learning
task: Spin-crossover metal-organic framework screening via quantile regression tree active learning
key_results: Random Forest model trained on 200-sized active-learning subset recovered ~82% of PBE-defined positives from noisy unrelaxed-geometry labels; identified new pSCO-105 collection
comments: Data-efficient strategy pragmatically addresses computational bottleneck, but only 82% recovery with two false negatives; negative-control tests confirm chemical meaningfulness but external validation lacking.

model_io.model: Quantile Regression Tree-based Active Learning selector
inputs: noisy adiabatic energy differences from unrelaxed geometries
selected MOFs with PBE-computed relaxed-geometry labels

hypotheses.hypothesis: Active learning on noisy unrelaxed data identifies SCO-relevant MOFs as accurately as full DFT screening
hypotheses.result: ~82% recovery of PBE positives; identified pSCO-105 high-confidence collection; negative-control tests show chemical relevance

title: Ontology-grounded nanotoxicity data federation with a provenance-aware knowledge graph and conformal prediction for antimicrobial hazard screening
task: Ontology-grounded nanotoxicity data federation with knowledge graph and conformal prediction for antimicrobial hazard screening
key_results: AUROC 0.819 ± 0.020 under 5-fold CV; split conformal prediction achieved marginal coverage 0.955, 0.929, 0.825 against targets 0.95, 0.90, 0.80; material-grouped CV reduced AUROC to 0.609 ± 0.098
comments: Rigorous semantic integration and provenance tracking with explicit uncertainty quantification, but severe generalization gap to unseen material classes (AUROC drop from 0.819 to 0.609) indicates fundamental feature-based limitations.

model_io.model: Data federation pipeline with eNanoMapper ontology
inputs: 6,588 MIC/MBC records from curated repositories and literature

hypotheses.hypothesis: Categorical experimental context carries stronger discriminative signal than physicochemical descriptors
hypotheses.result: Feature attribution shows experimental context dominance; material-grouped CV stress test reveals poor cross-material generalization (AUROC 0.609 ± 0.098)

title: Resilient UAV formation tracking using hybrid fractional-order terminal sliding mode control
task: Resilient UAV formation tracking using adaptive fractional-order terminal sliding mode control
key_results: Fractional-order leader achieves 85–92% reduction in integrated tracking error (IAE, ITAE); restricts horizontal position errors to ±0.01 m and reduces vertical deviation by >80% under 65% mass variation and stochastic disturbances
comments: Extensive numerical simulations demonstrate theoretical advantages, but findings are simulation-only without experimental flight validation; practical robustness claims require field testing.

model_io.model: Adaptive fractional-order nonsingular fast terminal sliding mode control (AFONFTSMC)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fractional-order modeling in leader dynamics enhances multi-agent coordination robustness
hypotheses.result: 85–92% IAE/ITAE reduction; convergence within 0.15 s under nominal conditions; <1.5 s disturbance recovery under severe uncertainty

title: RamanGPT maps bidirectionally between crystal structures and Raman spectra of inorganic materials
task: Bidirectional mapping between crystal structures and Raman spectra using deep learning
key_results: Forward model: 53.8% of 509 held-out materials reach cosine similarity ≥ 0.354; Inverse model: MAE of 1.13–2.14 Å for lattice parameters, 92.1% reduced-formula consistency vs. 17.1% retrieval baseline
comments: ALIGNN and fine-tuned DiffractGPT show promise but forward prediction captures only qualitative features; inverse model demonstrates substantial improvement over retrieval but requires formula conditioning.

inputs: crystal structures from 5,099 Computational Raman Database

outputs: predicted lattice parameters and reduced formula

hypotheses.hypothesis: GNN-based forward model predicts qualitative spectral features for unseen materials
hypotheses.result: 53.8% of held-out materials reach cosine similarity ≥ 0.354; qualitative agreement on 1T VSe₂ absent from training

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fine-tuned LLM inverse model outperforms formula-conditioned retrieval for structure recovery
hypotheses.result: 92.1% formula consistency vs. 17.1% retrieval baseline; MAE 1.13–2.14 Å

title: SPD-YOLO: a reliable model for imported supermarket products detection
